html:
Josip Broz Tito was the leader of communist Yugoslavia from 1945 to 1980, born in 1892 to a Croat father and Slovene mother in Kumrovec in northern Croatia.

A metalworker and soldier, he became a communist in Russia after World War I. In World War II he led the Partisans, who freed most of Yugoslavia themselves. He then built a federation of six republics under the slogan of brotherhood and unity. In 1948 he defied Stalin in the Tito Stalin split, opened the country to the West and developed workers' self management. With Nehru and Nasser he founded the Non-Aligned Movement. His death in 1980 left no one able to hold the federation together.
